# Copilot Instructions — LD.Infrastructure

## Project Description
Infrastructure layer (net10.0). Concrete implementations of all interfaces from `LD.Application`. Owns EF Core DbContext, Identity, JWT, repositories, interceptors, and background workers.

## Architectural Constraints

- All EF entity configurations go in `LdProyectDbContext.OnModelCreating()` — do NOT create `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` classes.
- All new repositories must be registered in `ConfigureServices.AddInfrastructureRepositories()`.
- All new services (auth, storage, etc.) must be registered in `ConfigureServices.AddInfrastructureServices()`.
- Never create a new `DbContext`; always use `LdProyectDbContext`.
- Never set audit fields manually — `AuditableEntitySaveChangesInterceptor` handles them.
- Migrations must be generated with: `dotnet ef migrations add <FeatureName> --project src/LD.Infrastructure --startup-project src/LD.Api`

## Repository Template

```csharp
// Repositories/FooRepository.cs
public class FooRepository : Repository<Foo>, IFooRepository
{
    public FooRepository(LdProyectDbContext context) : base(context) { }

    public async Task<List<Foo>> GetByClientAsync(int clientId)
        => await _context.Set<Foo>()
            .Where(f => f.ClientId == clientId && f.IsActive)
            .ToListAsync();
}
```

```csharp
// Interface in LD.Application/Common/Interfaces/Repository/IFooRepository.cs
public interface IFooRepository : IRepository<Foo>
{
    Task<List<Foo>> GetByClientAsync(int clientId);
}
```

```csharp
// Register in ConfigureServices.AddInfrastructureRepositories()
services.AddScoped<IFooRepository, FooRepository>();
```

## EF Configuration Example (in LdProyectDbContext.OnModelCreating)

```csharp
// Inside OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder builder):
builder.Entity<Foo>(entity =>
{
    entity.HasKey(e => e.FooId);
    entity.HasIndex(e => new { e.ClientId, e.Name }).IsUnique();
    entity.HasOne(e => e.Client)
          .WithMany(c => c.Foos)
          .HasForeignKey(e => e.ClientId);
});
```

## Migration Naming

Use a descriptive feature name:
```bash
# Good
dotnet ef migrations add AddFooTable --project src/LD.Infrastructure --startup-project src/LD.Api
dotnet ef migrations add UpdateAsnReceiptFields --project src/LD.Infrastructure --startup-project src/LD.Api

# Bad — do not use timestamps or numbers
dotnet ef migrations add Migration1
dotnet ef migrations add 20260512_Foo
```

## File/Folder Structure

```
Repositories/<Feature>Repository.cs       ← Extends Repository<T>
Services/Auth/                            ← AuthService, JwtTokenService, UserContextService
Services/Storage/                         ← LocalFileStorageService
Services/StandardLabel/                   ← StandardLabelService
Identity/ApplicationUser.cs / ApplicationRole.cs
Persistence/LdProyectDbContext.cs         ← ALL EF config here
Persistence/Interceptors/AuditableEntitySaveChangesInterceptor.cs
Persistence/Seeders/SeedUser.cs
Migrations/                               ← Generated by EF, do not edit
ConfigureServices.cs                      ← All DI registrations
```

## Naming Conventions

- Repository class: `<Entity>Repository`
- Repository interface: `I<Entity>Repository` (defined in `LD.Application`)
- Service class: `<Feature>Service`
- Service interface: `I<Feature>Service` (defined in `LD.Application`)

## What to Avoid

- Never create `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` files — all EF config in `OnModelCreating`
- Never edit migration `.cs` files manually — always regenerate
- Never add business logic to repositories (queries only, no if/else rules)
- Never call `SaveChangesAsync()` outside of repository methods
- Never bypass the `AuditableEntitySaveChangesInterceptor` by setting audit fields manually
